raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation In the current Eagle3 implementation, within a single `run_batch`, Decode executes in the order **Draft -> Verify -> DraftExtend**. As shown in the upper part of the figure, before the next `run_batch` can start, there is always a long **H<->D** wait that must complete. With Draft placed at the very beginning of `run_batch`, this waiting period cannot be well hidden, resulting in a Draft-and-Verify CPU dispatch bound. By reordering the Decode execution to **Verify -> DraftExtend -> Draft(Prefetch)**, better hiding can be achieved and the CPU bound eliminated. **The prerequisite is that the draft model itself does not trigger additional H<->D transfers.** For example, in `EAGLEDraftNpuGraphRunner._replay_graph`, DSA models do not need to read `seq_lens_cpu`, achieving the effect shown in the lower part of the figure. Non-DSA models, however, still need to read the updated (post-DraftExtend) `seq_lens_cpu`; otherwise, operator OOB issues or reduced acceptance rates would occur, and adding a synchronization inside Draft to work around this would completely negate the expected gains or even degrade performance further. ## Modifications **Core feature: DraftPrefetch -- moves Draft to right after the previous round's DraftExtend for better hiding.** 1. Draft is moved (copied) to execute after DraftExtend and renamed DraftPrefetch. Inside the method, a new batch is prepared with the updated `spec_info` and `seq_lens`, and its ForwardMode is set to `Decode`, then the entire original Draft logic runs once. The final outputs are the `topk_index` and `topk_p` derived from `draft_tokens`, which are assigned to `next_draft_input` and carried into the next `run_batch`. In the actual implementation, I reuse the existing batch by assigning attributes to it for the computation and restoring the original attributes afterwards. 2. Ahead of the Verify phase in a `run_batch`, PrepareVerifyInput now takes the place of Draft. It re-packs the inputs that were originally fed into Draft. 3. To bridge the Prefill and Decode stages (including the PD disaggregation scenario), PrepareVerifyInput must also be able to consume the `topk_index` and `topk_p` produced by Prefill. Therefore, Prefill's `topk_index` and `topk_p` are padded to satisfy the shape requirements. 4. To realize the performance gains, I added `pin_memory=True` at the H<->D trigger points during DraftPrefetch execution (`ForwardBatch.init_new`), or moved the operations onto the CPU (`EAGLEDraftNpuGraphRunner.can_run_graph`), so that the CPU operator dispatch remains fully asynchronous throughout the Verify -> DraftExtend -> DraftPrefetch process. 5. Added thorough argument validation for this feature. It is currently incompatible with speculative_adaptive, speculative_eagle_topk>1, speculative_num_steps<=1, multi_layer_eagle, and speculative_use_rejection_sampling; all of these combinations are rejected at startup. 6. Added test cases. While adding `pin_memory=True` to `ForwardBatch.init_new`, I found that the NPU platform does not yet implement `NpuSRTPlatform`, causing `is_pin_memory_available` to return the default value False set in `DeviceMixin`. Therefore, I filed a separate PR #36472 to implement `NpuSRTPlatform`. This PR builds on top of PR #36472 and requires it to be merged first. ## Accuracy Tests Theoretically, for dsa model, this feature will have absolutely no impact on its accuracy or accepted length, as seen in DeepSeek V3.2: ### Before: accept length: 2.69 tpot: 85.20 benchmark duration: 97.34 ### After: accept length: 2.69 tpot: 80.60 benchmark duration: 82.72 ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### H20 dsv3.2 (Layer pruning) prof Before: After: ### Ascend A3 dsv3.2-w8a8 prof Before: After: ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 8. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #33855566683](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33855566683) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #33855566549](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33855566549) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.

Hi @author, thanks for this PR! We ported it onto our deployment and want to share a profiling finding that may be useful.

  Setup: Qwen3.5-122B (hybrid GDN + MoE), PD-disaggregated decode side, NEXTN spec with --speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3, TP=4 + DP=4.

  Behavior: correct — spec_accept_length and the acceptance histogram are unchanged vs the same build with the env flag off, server is stable. But end-to-end TPS is on par with baseline, so we profiled with the built-in torch profiler to find out why.

  What the trace shows:

  1. ✅ The next-round draft is genuinely pre-executed. draft_forward_zero_bubble's kernels land on a separate CUDA stream (Stream B) and on the GPU timeline they overlap with the current iteration's verify/MoE on Stream A. 
  2. ⚠️ But right after Stream B's draft finishes, the GPU goes sparse for a noticeable window before the next iteration's verify can start. During that window the CPU is busy with:
    - sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py:47 build_tree_kernel_efficient
    - sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info_v2.py:219 prepare_for_v2_verify
  Only after these CPU steps finish do we see the next iteration's verify kernels launch. 
  3. Quantitative: the overlapped draft window is ~180 µs. The end-to-end iteration period is essentially unchanged vs baseline. So the bubble didn't disappear — it transformed: the ~180 µs of draft GPU work was lifted out of the critical path, but the CPU build_tree + prepare_for_v2_verify segment underneath was already roughly the same width, so the GPU is still gated on it. Net wall-clock ≈ baseline.

  Question: Does this match what you'd expect to see? Is there anything in my reading of the trace, my port of the PR, or my measurement methodology that I might be getting wrong, or pieces I'm missing?
   Any pointers on what to double-check would be appreciated.

Thanks for the thorough profiling — a few observations:

**1. On the bubble:** The primary goal of this feature is to eliminate the CPU dispatch bottleneck between `draft_extend` and `draft`, and your trace confirms that's working. On NPU I've seen the remaining draft↔verify gap fully hidden by increasing the draft count, though on high-performance GPUs the gain may be less pronounced since the gap is narrower to begin with.

**2. On acceptance rate:** You mentioned acceptance rate is unchanged, which is a bit surprising. This feature intentionally skips (or defers) the `seq_lens_cpu` sync to avoid putting a CPU round-trip back into the critical path between `draft_extend` and `draft`. For non-DSA models that still rely on `seq_lens_cpu`, I'd expect some acceptance rate impact. Are the numbers truly identical with the flag on vs. off? This feature is a natural fit for DSA models like DeepSeek-V3.2, whose MTP doesn't depend on `seq_lens_cpu` at all.

**3. On flat TPS:** Looking at your trace, the draft GPU time is ~1.3 ms, and the restore-before-verify step introduces ~1.2 ms of CPU-bound work — consistent with your conclusion. On H20 with a pruned DeepSeek-V3.2, I measured a reduction in total time from `draft_extend` to the next `target` with the flag on. If that window is unchanged in your setup, then indeed there's no net gain.

**Summary:**
- The feature eliminates the `draft_extend`↔`draft` bubble, but the restore-before-verify step adds CPU overhead that can become the new bottleneck. 
- Increasing the draft count can mask the remaining gap, but if draft quality is low this may backfire — needs case-by-case evaluation.
- It's best suited for DSA models; other models may see acceptance rate degradation from the deferred `seq_lens_cpu` sync.
- I'll look into optimizing the restore-before-verify step on my side.

This pull request implements the 'Spec V2 Zero Bubble' feature for speculative decoding, introducing asynchronous drafting logic and environment variable controls. Feedback identifies critical bugs when `topk > 1`, including tensor dimension mismatches during concatenation and incorrect tree structure construction. Additionally, a bug in the pinned memory device check for indexed strings was noted, along with a recommendation to re-anchor hidden states to the target model for better accuracy.

The string comparison `str(device) == "cuda"` (and similarly for `"npu"`) will fail if the device string includes an index, such as `"cuda:0"`. This is a common format for device strings in SGLang. This will cause the function to return `False` incorrectly, disabling pinned memory optimizations for indexed devices.

```suggestion
    device_type = str(device).split(":")[0]
    if device_type == "cuda":
        return _is_cuda
    if device_type == "npu":
        return _is_npu
```

The logic for constructing `score_list` and `token_list` is incorrect for `topk > 1`. 

`tree_info[0]` has a shape of `(batch_size, 1, speculative_num_steps * topk)` because it was initialized from a concatenated tensor in `select_top_k_tokens(0, ...)`. 
By iterating `range(self.speculative_num_steps)` and taking `tree_info[0][:, :, i]`, the code only extracts the probability of the first token for each step, completely ignoring the other `topk - 1` tokens. This breaks the EAGLE tree structure which relies on multiple candidates per step.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces the `SGLANG_SPEC_V2_ZERO_BUBBLE` feature to optimize speculative decoding, specifically targeting the EAGLE worker. The implementation includes a new `draft_zero_bubble` execution path, logic to skip `seq_lens_cpu` synchronization for improved performance on compatible architectures like DeepSeek-V3.2, and memory pinning optimizations for several GPU-bound tensors. The reviewer feedback highlights a misleading warning message regarding the synchronization requirements of the new feature and identifies an opportunity to reduce code duplication by extracting shared result-organizing logic into a helper method.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The first sentence of this warning message seems misleading. It states that the `spec_v2_zero_bubble` feature "requires seq_lens_cpu synchronization", but the goal of this feature and the implementation (commented-out sync in `draft_zero_bubble`) is to *avoid* this synchronization to improve performance.

To avoid confusion, I suggest rephrasing the warning to clarify that the feature *skips* the synchronization and explain the trade-off. For example:

"`spec_v2_zero_bubble` is enabled. This feature improves performance by skipping `seq_lens_cpu` synchronization (GPU->CPU copy) during the draft phase. This is optimal for models like DeepSeek-V3.2 that do not depend on `seq_lens_cpu`. For models that do, skipping this sync may affect acceptance length, though it can be re-enabled in the code for correctness at the cost of some performance."

detail.body: ## Motivation In the current Eagle3 implementation, within a single `run_batch`, Decode executes in the order **Draft -> Verify -> DraftExtend**. As shown in the upper part of the figure, before the next `run_batch` can start, there is always a long **H<->D** wait that must complete. With Draft placed at the very beginning of `run_batch`, this waiting period cannot be well hidden, resulting in a Draft-and-Verify CPU dispatch bound. By reordering the Decode execution to **Verify -> DraftExtend -> Draft(Prefetch)**, better hiding can be achieved and the CPU bound eliminated. **The prerequisite is that the draft model itself does not trigger additional H<->D transfers.** For example, in `EAGLEDraftNpuGraphRunner._replay_graph`, DSA models do not need to read `seq_lens_cpu`, achieving the effect shown in the lower part of the figure. Non-DSA models, however, still need to read the updated (post-DraftExtend) `seq_lens_cpu`; otherwise, operator OOB issues or reduced acceptance rates would occur, and adding a synchronization inside Draft to work around this would completely negate the expected gains or even degrade performance further. ## Modifications **Core feature: DraftPrefetch -- moves Draft to right after the previous round's DraftExtend for better hiding.** 1. Draft is moved (copied) to execute after DraftExtend and renamed DraftPrefetch. Inside the method, a new batch is prepared with the updated `spec_info` and `seq_lens`, and its ForwardMode is set to `Decode`, then the entire original Draft logic runs once. The final outputs are the `topk_index` and `topk_p` derived from `draft_tokens`, which are assigned to `next_draft_input` and carried into the next `run_batch`. In the actual implementation, I reuse the existing batch by assigning attributes to it for the computation and restoring the original attributes afterwards. 2. Ahead of the Verify phase in a `run_batch`, PrepareVerifyInput now takes the place of Draft. It re-packs the inputs that were originally fed into Draft. 3. To bridge the Prefill and Decode stages (including the PD disaggregation scenario), PrepareVerifyInput must also be able to consume the `topk_index` and `topk_p` produced by Prefill. Therefore, Prefill's `topk_index` and `topk_p` are padded to satisfy the shape requirements. 4. To realize the performance gains, I added `pin_memory=True` at the H<->D trigger points during DraftPrefetch execution (`ForwardBatch.init_new`), or moved the operations onto the CPU (`EAGLEDraftNpuGraphRunner.can_run_graph`), so that the CPU operator dispatch remains fully asynchronous throughout the Verify -> DraftExtend -> DraftPrefetch process. 5. Added thorough argument validation for this feature. It is currently incompatible with speculative_adaptive, speculative_eagle_topk>1, speculative_num_steps<=1, multi_layer_eagle, and speculative_use_rejection_sampling; all of these combinations are rejected at startup. 6. Added test cases. While adding `pin_memory=True` to `ForwardBatch.init_new`, I found that the NPU platform does not yet implement `NpuSRTPlatform`, causing `is_pin_memory_available` to return the default value False set in `DeviceMixin`. Therefore, I filed a separate PR #36472 to implement `NpuSRTPlatform`. This PR builds on top of PR #36472 and requires it to be merged first. ## Accuracy Tests Theoretically, for dsa model, this feature will have absolutely no impact on its accuracy or accepted length, as seen in DeepSeek V3.2: ### Before: accept length: 2.69 tpot: 85.20 benchmark duration: 97.34 ### After: accept length: 2.69 tpot: 80.60 benchmark duration: 82.72 ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### H20 dsv3.2 (Layer pruning) prof Before: After: ### Ascend A3 dsv3.2-w8a8 prof Before: After: ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. +"""--enable-draft-prefetch: pre-run the next round's draft after draft_extend.
+
+With draft prefetch, EAGLEWorkerV2 pre-runs the next round's draft decode
+back-to-back with this round's draft_extend (on the forward stream), and
+pre-concatenates the per-step topk into the next draft input. The next decode
+round then builds its verify input from the pre-concatenated candidate chain
+(prepare_verify_input_for_draft_prefetch) instead of re-running the draft.
+This file guards that the optimization is lossless:
+
+  - greedy parity vs a non-spec reference server (SpecParityKit);
+  - acceptance length / verify bookkeeping (SpecCorrectnessKit);
+  - gsm8k quality + accept length (SpecAccuracyKit);
+  - radix / abort / grammar features with a strict memory check -- a leak from
+    the extra pre-run draft would trip it (SpecFeatureKit).
+
+Constraint surface (enforced by _check_draft_prefetch): EAGLE family (this
+file exercises EAGLE3), topk=1, num_steps > 1, non-adaptive, no rejection
+sampling. The unit tests for that validation live in
+test/registered/unit/spec/test_spec_draft_prefetch_args.py.

Thanks for the thorough profiling — a few observations:

**1. On the bubble:** The primary goal of this feature is to eliminate the CPU dispatch bottleneck between `draft_extend` and `draft`, and your trace confirms that's working. On NPU I've seen the remaining draft↔verify gap fully hidden by increasing the draft count, though on high-performance GPUs the gain may be less pronounced since the gap is narrower to begin with.

**2. On acceptance rate:** You mentioned acceptance rate is unchanged, which is a bit surprising. This feature intentionally skips (or defers) the `seq_lens_cpu` sync to avoid putting a CPU round-trip back into the critical path between `draft_extend` and `draft`. For non-DSA models that still rely on `seq_lens_cpu`, I'd expect some acceptance rate impact. Are the numbers truly identical with the flag on vs. off? This feature is a natural fit for DSA models like DeepSeek-V3.2, whose MTP doesn't depend on `seq_lens_cpu` at all.

**3. On flat TPS:** Looking at your trace, the draft GPU time is ~1.3 ms, and the restore-before-verify step introduces ~1.2 ms of CPU-bound work — consistent with your conclusion. On H20 with a pruned DeepSeek-V3.2, I measured a reduction in total time from `draft_extend` to the next `target` with the flag on. If that window is unchanged in your setup, then indeed there's no net gain.

**Summary:**
- The feature eliminates the `draft_extend`↔`draft` bubble, but the restore-before-verify step adds CPU overhead that can become the new bottleneck. 
- Increasing the draft count can mask the remaining gap, but if draft quality is low this may backfire — needs case-by-case evaluation.
- It's best suited for DSA models; other models may see acceptance rate degradation from the deferred `seq_lens_cpu` sync.
- I'll look into optimizing the restore-before-verify step on my side.

## Code Review

This pull request implements the 'Spec V2 Zero Bubble' feature for speculative decoding, introducing asynchronous drafting logic and environment variable controls. Feedback identifies critical bugs when `topk > 1`, including tensor dimension mismatches during concatenation and incorrect tree structure construction. Additionally, a bug in the pinned memory device check for indexed strings was noted, along with a recommendation to re-anchor hidden states to the target model for better accuracy.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces the `SGLANG_SPEC_V2_ZERO_BUBBLE` feature to optimize speculative decoding, specifically targeting the EAGLE worker. The implementation includes a new `draft_zero_bubble` execution path, logic to skip `seq_lens_cpu` synchronization for improved performance on compatible architectures like DeepSeek-V3.2, and memory pinning optimizations for several GPU-bound tensors. The reviewer feedback highlights a misleading warning message regarding the synchronization requirements of the new feature and identifies an opportunity to reduce code duplication by extracting shared result-organizing logic into a helper method.
